suggestions.description: The Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) is significantly delayed because the LCP image element is incorrectly configured with `loading="lazy"`. This defers the image request until late in the page load, after the layout is complete, instead of fetching it immediately. The LCP element, an `` with a `src` attribute containing `media_155e651a6c3ae1fb32f0b99f85d72e2e3d77f3364.webp`, has a render time of over 2.9 seconds.
suggestions.implementation:
In the project's JavaScript, within the `loadEager` or `decorateMain` function in `scripts.js`, programmatically find the main hero image (typically the first `` in the `
` element). Set its `loading` attribute to `"eager"` and add the `fetchpriority="high"` attribute. This instructs the browser to download this critical resource immediately with high priority.
suggestions.title: Prioritize the LCP Image Request to Improve LCP

suggestions.description:
The Ensighten Tag Manager script (`nexus.ensighten.com/.../Bootstrap.js`) is a major performance bottleneck. It initiates over 100 subsequent requests and executes long-running JavaScript tasks (up to 533ms) on the main thread. This blocks rendering, delays LCP, and is a root cause of the poor Interaction to Next Paint (INP) score of 304ms.

Several large, non-essential third-party scripts for chat, analytics, and security are loaded early in the page load process. This includes the Alive5 chat widget, Google Tag Manager, Google reCAPTCHA, and Facebook Events. These scripts consume significant network bandwidth and block the main thread, contributing to high Total Blocking Time, poor INP, and LCP delays.
suggestions.implementation:
- In `scripts.js`, locate the loading and initialization logic for the Ensighten script (`Bootstrap.js`). Move this logic into the `loadDelayed()` function. This will defer its execution until after the page has finished rendering and become interactive, removing it from the critical path for both initial rendering and user interaction.
- In `scripts.js`, locate the initialization logic for the Alive5 chat widget (`alive5.com`), Google Tag Manager (`googletagmanager.com`), Google reCAPTCHA (`recaptcha`), and Facebook Events (`fbevents.js`). Move the function calls that load and initialize these services into the `loadDelayed()` function. This will ensure they only execute after the main page content has loaded and is interactive.
suggestions.title: Defer the Ensighten Tag Manager to Improve INP and LCP

suggestions.description: A significant layout shift, contributing a large portion of the page's 0.31 CLS score, occurs on mobile devices when the site header is loaded asynchronously and inserted into the page. This pushes all subsequent content down by approximately 45px. The element identified as shifting is `.mobile-nav__header-container`.
suggestions.implementation: In the project's main stylesheet (`styles.css`), apply a `min-height` of `45px` (or the exact measured height of the rendered header) to the selector for the header's placeholder container. This will reserve the necessary vertical space before the header content is rendered, preventing the layout shift.
suggestions.title: Reserve Space for the Asynchronously Loaded Mobile Header to Fix CLS

suggestions.description: An element with the class `.global-alert` is inserted asynchronously into the page after the initial render, causing a massive layout shift of 0.44. This happens because no space is reserved for the element, and when it appears, it pushes all subsequent content down, creating a poor user experience.
suggestions.implementation: In the block's CSS file (e.g., `/blocks/global-alert/global-alert.css`), apply a fixed `min-height` to the `.global-alert` selector. The height should match the final rendered height of the alert to reserve the necessary vertical space before the component's content is loaded and rendered, preventing the content shift.
suggestions.title: Reserve space for the Global Alert to prevent major layout shift

suggestions.description: Over 1.8 MB of JavaScript from analytics, advertising, social media, and security vendors is loaded and executed early. This creates long tasks (up to 1506ms) that block the main thread, severely degrading Interaction to Next Paint (INP) and delaying the Largest Contentful Paint (LCP). Key offenders include scripts from googletagmanager.com, connect.facebook.net, and other large, unidentified bundles.
suggestions.implementation: In `/scripts/scripts.js`, move the loading of all non-essential scripts from the `loadEager` phase to the `loadDelayed` function. This applies to scripts for analytics, ads, social widgets, session replay, and marketing. Specifically target scripts from `googletagmanager.com`, `connect.facebook.net`, `techlab-cdn.com`, `OneTrust`, and large widget bundles like `car-trawler-widget` and `consider_widgets`.
suggestions.title: Defer non-essential and third-party JavaScript to improve interactivity and LCP

suggestions.description: A large, 306 KB image (`.../adobe/assets/...cf408295...`) that is likely the page's Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) element is being loaded with a `Low` fetch priority. This causes a long download delay (over 5 seconds), which directly and significantly harms the LCP metric.
suggestions.implementation: Identify the `` element for the LCP image (`/adobe/assets/...cf408295...`). Add the `fetchpriority="high"` and `loading="eager"` attributes directly to its HTML tag. If the tag cannot be modified directly in AEM, use JavaScript in the `loadEager` function within `scripts.js` to find the element and set `img.fetchPriority = 'high'` and `img.loading = 'eager'`.
suggestions.title: Prioritize the LCP image to accelerate rendering

suggestions.description: The main document request for https://www.vitamix.com is subject to a redirect chain that adds a significant delay before the browser can even begin to fetch page resources. This directly harms TTFB and pushes back the entire rendering process, delaying LCP by an estimated 750ms.
suggestions.implementation: Review your server (e.g., Apache, Nginx) or CDN (e.g., Akamai, Cloudflare) configuration to eliminate the redirect chain. Ensure that a request to the canonical URL 'https://www.vitamix.com' directly serves the final HTML document with a 200 OK status code, avoiding any intermediate 301 or 302 responses.
suggestions.title: Eliminate server-side redirects to improve TTFB and LCP

suggestions.description:
A large, 2.4MB JavaScript file is loaded synchronously in the `<head>`, blocking page rendering and causing a 563ms long task that freezes the main thread. This script (path ending in '/0k6bBwB') is the primary performance bottleneck, delaying LCP by over 1000ms and severely impacting INP.

Multiple non-critical stylesheets, including `/styles/lazy-styles.css`, `/styles/fonts.css`, and several block-specific CSS files (e.g., `/blocks/footer/footer.css`), are included as render-blocking resources in the `<head>`. This blocks the browser from painting any pixels until all of these files are downloaded and parsed, delaying LCP and FCP.
suggestions.implementation:
- Identify the purpose of the obfuscated script located at the path ending in '.../cGZ7yZaTFz/.../0k6bBwB'. As it is not critical for initial render, move its loading mechanism into the `loadDelayed` function within `/scripts/scripts.js`. This will defer its execution until after the page is interactive, removing it from the critical path.
- Modify your page template and logic in `/scripts/scripts.js`. Ensure only essential, critical-path CSS (e.g., `/styles/styles.css`) is loaded synchronously in the `<head>`. Load secondary stylesheets like `/styles/lazy-styles.css` and `/styles/fonts.css` asynchronously by appending `<link>` elements within the `loadLazy` function in `scripts.js`.
suggestions.title: Defer large, render-blocking third-party script to unblock rendering

suggestions.description: The LCP image (e.g., '/media_18838c424d602fadcdf84d8c558387bb45ac32bb9.png') is not being prioritized for download, causing its render to be delayed until 3060ms. It is being treated as a normal-priority resource instead of a critical one, delaying LCP by an estimated 400-500ms.
suggestions.implementation: Within the `loadEager` function in `/scripts/scripts.js`, identify the primary hero image element (e.g., by targeting 'main > div:first-child img'). Programmatically set its attributes `loading = 'eager'` and `fetchpriority = 'high'` to ensure the browser downloads it immediately with high priority.
suggestions.title: Prioritize the LCP image download with fetchpriority='high'

suggestions.description: The initial request to `https://evidentscientific.com` is met with a 302 redirect to `/en/`. This adds a full network round-trip before the browser can begin fetching the actual page content, delaying TTFB, FCP, and LCP by an estimated 750ms.
suggestions.implementation: Configure the CDN (Fastly) or web server to serve the default language content (from the `/en/` path) directly from the root path (`/`). This will eliminate the redirect and allow the browser to start downloading the HTML document immediately, significantly improving load times.
suggestions.title: Eliminate the initial domain redirect to improve server response time

suggestions.description: Over 10MB of third-party JavaScript for analytics, marketing, and consent management (e.g., Google Tag Manager, OneTrust, Baidu, Facebook) are loaded synchronously in the `<head>` or eagerly via JavaScript. This causes significant main-thread blocking, with long tasks over 300ms, delaying interactivity and contributing to a poor INP score.
suggestions.implementation: To align with AEM EDS best practices, remove all third-party `<script>` tags (e.g., `hm.baidu.com`, `cdn.cookielaw.org`, and others for Taboola, Clarity, LinkedIn) from the HTML `<head>`. Consolidate their initialization within the `loadDelayed` function in `/scripts/scripts.js`. This will postpone their download and execution until after the page is interactive, freeing up the main thread during the critical loading phase.
suggestions.title: Defer all non-essential third-party scripts to fix main-thread blocking

suggestions.description: A long animation frame at the very beginning of the page load blocks the main thread for 657ms. This long task occurs within the 'loadEager' phase of `scripts.js` and severely delays the initial render (FCP/LCP) and prevents user interaction, harming INP.
suggestions.implementation: Investigate the JavaScript executing in the `loadEager` function within `/scripts/scripts.js`. Identify the code responsible for the 657ms task and break it into smaller, asynchronous chunks. Use techniques like `setTimeout(..., 0)` or the `scheduler.yield()` API between logical units of work to yield control back to the browser's main thread, allowing rendering and user input to be processed.
suggestions.title: Break up initial long-running JavaScript task to improve LCP and INP

suggestions.description: The server takes over 1.45 seconds (p75) to respond to the initial page request, which severely delays the entire page load. Additional analysis shows that static assets like SVGs and CSS files also have a high Time to First Byte (TTFB) of ~300ms, indicating a systemic caching issue on the origin server or CDN.
suggestions.implementation: Investigate and optimize the AEM Dispatcher caching configuration. The goal is to ensure the main HTML document is cached effectively to reduce the 1.45s TTFB to under 800ms. Additionally, configure the dispatcher to serve all static assets (`.css`, `.js`, `.svg`, etc.) from its cache with an appropriate `Cache-Control` header, reducing their individual TTFB to under 50ms.
suggestions.title: Improve Slow Server Response Time (TTFB)

suggestions.description: The Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) element, the main hero image (`media_1909af9f0f670fb59954f6db4e8cf036caf81f9c9.png`), is delayed by over 900ms because it is not prioritized correctly. It is likely being lazy-loaded and has a low fetch priority, preventing the browser from discovering and downloading it early.
suggestions.implementation: In the HTML, locate the `` tag for the hero image (`.../media_1909af9f0f670fb59954f6db4e8cf036caf81f9c9.png`). Remove the `loading="lazy"` attribute and add `fetchpriority="high"`. This will instruct the browser to download this critical image immediately with high priority.
suggestions.title: Prioritize the LCP Image to Reduce Load Delay

suggestions.description: A 1555ms long task freezes the main thread at the very start of page load. This extremely long script execution blocks all rendering, delaying the First Contentful Paint and Largest Contentful Paint by over 1.5 seconds and making the page completely unresponsive.
suggestions.implementation: Use browser developer tools to profile the page load and identify the specific JavaScript function causing the 1555ms block at page start. Refactor this long-running script by breaking it into smaller chunks that execute for less than 50ms each. Use techniques like `setTimeout`, `requestIdleCallback`, or `async`/`await` to yield control back to the main thread between chunks.
suggestions.title: Break Up Initial 1.5-Second Main-Thread Blocking Task

suggestions.description: The site's Time to First Byte (TTFB) is severely impacting LCP, with backend requests for essential JavaScript components taking over 870ms. This indicates a major bottleneck on the AEM origin server, as CDN caching is also failing for these resources.
suggestions.implementation: Investigate and optimize the AEM publish tier's performance for serving block-specific JavaScript files like `product-details/components/deferredScript.js`, `messageRender.js`, and `gallery.js`. Focus on the server-side logic (Sling Models, JCR queries) that generates these dynamic resources to reduce the high 'Wait' time identified in network requests. Ensure proper CDN cache headers are set to prevent cache misses for these assets.
suggestions.title: Optimize AEM Server Response Time (TTFB) for Component Scripts

suggestions.description: The Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) image is incorrectly configured with `loading="lazy"`, which de-prioritizes its download and critically delays the LCP metric by over 800ms. The browser discovers and loads other resources before starting the download for the most important visual element on the page.
suggestions.implementation: In the JavaScript responsible for the main hero image (likely `/blocks/product-details/components/gallery.js` or a general function in `scripts.js`), programmatically update the LCP image element's attributes during the 'loadEager' phase. Change `loading` from `"lazy"` to `"eager"` and add `fetchpriority="high"`. This will instruct the browser to download the image immediately with high priority.
suggestions.title: Prioritize LCP Image Loading by Removing `loading="lazy"`

suggestions.description: Non-critical stylesheets for fonts, lazy-loaded content, the header, and the footer are loaded as render-blocking resources in the document `<head>`. This forces the browser to download and parse them before rendering any content, unnecessarily delaying FCP and LCP.
suggestions.implementation: In the main HTML template, remove the `<link rel="stylesheet">` tags for `/styles/lazy-styles.css`, `/styles/fonts.css`, `/blocks/header/header.css`, and `/blocks/footer/footer.css`. Modify `scripts.js` to load these stylesheets asynchronously within the `loadLazy` function, after the initial page content has rendered.
suggestions.title: Defer Non-Critical CSS to Unblock Rendering

suggestions.description:
Critical static assets like `scripts.js` and `styles.css` are being served with a very short cache lifetime (`max-age=60`). This causes frequent CDN cache misses and high Time to First Byte (TTFB) for resources essential to rendering the page, slowing down the entire page load.

The header and footer HTML fragments are being fetched asynchronously directly from the AEM publish origin (`publish-p25603-e86971.adobeaemcloud.com`), bypassing the CDN. This results in a high TTFB of over 500ms for these fragments, delaying their rendering and potentially causing layout shifts.
suggestions.implementation:
- Update the AEM dispatcher or CDN configuration to set a long-lived `Cache-Control` header for immutable, static assets like CSS and JS (e.g., `Cache-Control: max-age=31536000, immutable`). This will ensure browsers and the CDN can cache these files effectively, reducing TTFB and server load on subsequent visits.
- In `scripts.js`, locate the `fetch` calls responsible for loading the header and footer fragments. Modify the target URL to use the public CDN domain (`main--notice--softbankbtob.aem.page`) instead of the internal AEM origin. This change will allow the CDN (Fastly) to cache the fragment HTML, serving it with a low TTFB on subsequent page loads.
suggestions.title: Increase Cache Lifetime for Static Assets to Improve TTFB

suggestions.description: Multiple heavy third-party scripts for analytics and marketing (Google Tag Manager, Adobe DTM, Treasure Data, Marketo) are loaded early, executing long tasks (up to 1137ms) that block the main thread. This significantly delays LCP and degrades interactivity (INP). For instance, gtm.js executes over 1.5MB of code before LCP.
suggestions.implementation: In `scripts.js`, remove the initialization logic for all non-essential third-party scripts from the eager-loading phase. Move the loading calls for Google Tag Manager (GTM), Adobe DTM/Launch, Treasure Data SDK, and Marketo into the `loadDelayed()` function. This will postpone their execution until after the page has rendered and is interactive, freeing up the main thread for critical tasks.
suggestions.title: Defer Third-Party Marketing and Analytics Scripts to Unblock the Main Thread

suggestions.description:
The page loads numerous render-blocking CSS files in the `<head>`, including styles that should be loaded asynchronously like `global-nav.css`, `header.css`, and even `lazy-styles.css`. This creates a long request chain that blocks rendering and significantly delays the Largest Contentful Paint (LCP).

Three large custom font files (`NotoSansJP-*`), totaling over 1.8 MB, are loaded on the critical rendering path. Their `@font-face` declarations are located in a synchronously loaded stylesheet, which blocks rendering and delays LCP.
suggestions.implementation:
- Consolidate all essential CSS rules required for the initial, above-the-fold viewport into the main `styles.css` file. Move all other styles—including those for the header/navigation (`global-nav.css`), footer, and other below-the-fold components—into `lazy-styles.css`. Ensure `lazy-styles.css` is loaded asynchronously via the `loadLazy` function in `scripts.js` and is not included as a blocking `<link>` tag in the document `<head>`.
- Move the `@font-face` declarations for the 'NotoSansJP' fonts from the critical `styles.css` file to the asynchronously loaded `lazy-styles.css`. This ensures the large font files are downloaded after the initial page content has rendered, unblocking the critical path.
suggestions.title: Consolidate and Defer Non-Critical CSS to Unblock Rendering

suggestions.description: The OneTrust cookie consent banner is injected into the page dynamically without any reserved space. This causes a large layout shift (reported CLS of 0.545) as it pushes down existing content, such as '#onetrust-policy-text', by nearly 300px.
suggestions.implementation: In the initial HTML document, add a placeholder element where the OneTrust banner is expected to be injected by its script. Style this placeholder with a `min-height` of approximately 300px to reserve the required vertical space, preventing the layout shift when the banner content loads.
suggestions.title: Reserve space for the OneTrust cookie banner to prevent layout shift

suggestions.description: Multiple images across the site are missing explicit `width` and `height` attributes. This causes significant layout shifts (contributing to a CLS score of 0.246) when the images load and push content down, as the browser does not know how much space to reserve for them beforehand.
suggestions.implementation: Modify the AEM components responsible for rendering images to ensure they always include `width` and `height` attributes on all `` tags. This action will allow the browser to reserve the correct amount of space in the layout before the image file is downloaded, stabilizing the layout and preventing content shifts.
suggestions.title: Add width and height attributes to images to prevent layout shifts

suggestions.description: When custom web fonts are loaded, they replace fallback system fonts of a different size. This discrepancy causes text to reflow and contributes significantly to the site's high CLS score, with observed shifts up to 101px in height.
suggestions.implementation: In your main stylesheet (e.g., `styles.css`), use the `@font-face` rule to define a local fallback font. Apply the `size-adjust` CSS property (along with `ascent-override`, `descent-override`, and `line-gap-override` if needed) to this fallback font to precisely match its metrics to the primary web font. This minimizes the size difference and reduces the layout shift when the font swap occurs.
suggestions.title: Adjust fallback font metrics to prevent layout shifts during font swapping

suggestions.description:
The main thread is blocked early in the page load by long sequential request chains for analytics and tracking. This is initiated by /scripts/tms.js, which loads in the `loadEager` phase. This single script triggers over 9 seconds of blocking activity from Google Analytics and Facebook, delaying the LCP by an estimated 2 seconds and severely impacting page interactivity.

Several heavy third-party scripts are executing long tasks on the main thread, causing high Total Blocking Time and poor interactivity (INP). Specifically, the accessibility script from `acsbapp.com` causes a 458ms long task, and analytics scripts from the `/metrics/` path cause a 516ms long task. These scripts also contain significant amounts of unused code.
suggestions.implementation:
- In the main `scripts/scripts.js` file, locate the code that loads `/scripts/tms.js`. Move this code from the `loadEager` function to the `loadDelayed` function. This will defer its execution, along with all downstream analytics and marketing tags, until after the page is fully loaded and interactive.
- In `scripts/scripts.js`, find the initialization logic for the accessibility script (`acsbapp.com/apps/app/dist/js/app.js`) and the first-party analytics scripts loaded from the `/metrics/` path. Move this logic into the `loadDelayed` function to ensure these scripts only execute after the page is fully loaded and interactive.
suggestions.title: Defer loading of tms.js to improve LCP and INP

suggestions.description:
A request for the HTML fragment at `/fragments/search.plain.html` is taking over 7.6 seconds to complete. This is a severe server-side bottleneck that blocks the rendering of page content and significantly delays the LCP.

The initial request to `https://www.unes.it` goes through a redirect chain before landing on the final page, adding approximately 750ms of latency. This delays the Time to First Byte (TTFB) and consequently the entire rendering process, including FCP and LCP.

Core static assets, including the main document, `styles.css`, and `scripts.js`, are frequently missing the CDN cache (`X-Cache: MISS`). This forces requests to go to the origin server, significantly increasing load times for TTFB, FCP, and LCP. This is a fundamental performance issue.
suggestions.implementation:
- Investigate the backend performance of the AEM component or query that generates the `/fragments/search.plain.html` fragment on the AEM publish tier. Optimize the server-side code, database queries, or implement appropriate caching strategies (e.g., AEM Dispatcher caching) to reduce its response time to under 500ms.
- Review the server (e.g., Apache, Nginx) and CDN (Fastly) configurations to remove the redirect chain. Ensure that the initial request resolves directly to the final destination URL (e.g., `https://www.unes.it/it/`) in a single step. This often involves correcting HTTP-to-HTTPS or non-www-to-www rules.
- Investigate the Fastly CDN configuration to determine why critical, static resources are not being cached effectively. Check for incorrect `Cache-Control` headers, `Vary` headers that include user-specific values, or `Set-Cookie` response headers on cacheable assets. Also, ensure query string parameters are not unnecessarily breaking the cache key. The goal is to achieve a high cache HIT ratio for all static assets.
suggestions.title: Optimize slow server response for search.plain.html fragment

suggestions.description: An extremely long JavaScript task is blocking the main thread for 1844ms at the very start of the page load. This severe blocking prevents the browser from rendering content or responding to user input, critically impacting INP and delaying LCP. The task appears to originate from logic within the `loadEager` phase of `scripts.js`.
suggestions.implementation: In `scripts.js`, identify the function or loop within the `loadEager` phase responsible for the 1844ms long task. Refactor this code to break the work into smaller chunks. Use `setTimeout(..., 0)` or the `scheduler.yield()` API between chunks to yield control back to the main thread, allowing it to process rendering updates and user interactions.
suggestions.title: Break up 1.8-second JavaScript task during initial load

suggestions.description:
The Osano Consent Management Platform script (osano.js) is a primary performance bottleneck. It's over 1.2MB, loaded synchronously, and executes a long task (~280ms) that blocks the main thread. This severely delays the First Contentful Paint and Largest Contentful Paint, with an estimated impact of over 900ms.

The third-party chat widget from TalkDesk is downloading over 1.8MB of JavaScript and CSS during initial page load. Much of this code is unused, and its execution contributes to long tasks, degrading interactivity (INP) and blocking the main thread.

A synchronous script for the Microsoft Authentication Library (`msal-browser.js`) is included in the document `<head>` without an `async` or `defer` attribute. This makes it a render-blocking resource, unnecessarily delaying the initial page render.
suggestions.implementation:
- To remove this script from the critical rendering path, move its initialization logic into the `loadDelayed` function within `/scripts/scripts.js`. This will defer its loading and execution until after the page has rendered and become interactive. Note: Test thoroughly to ensure consent functionality is not compromised by this change.
- Implement a facade pattern by replacing the chat widget with a static 'Chat' button and load the TalkDesk scripts only when a user clicks this button. As a simpler alternative, move all TalkDesk script initialization logic into the `loadDelayed` function in `/scripts/scripts.js` to defer it until after the main page content is loaded.
- Remove the blocking `<script src=".../msal-browser.js">` tag from the HTML `<head>`. Load this script asynchronously by moving its initialization into the `loadDelayed` function in `/scripts/scripts.js`.
suggestions.title: Defer the Osano Consent Management Platform Script

suggestions.description: The site's Time to First Byte (TTFB) is very high at 1.03s (p75), far above the 'good' threshold. Evidence from server headers (`X-Cache: MISS`) shows that critical resources, including the main HTML document and core JavaScript/CSS files, are not being consistently served from the Fastly CDN cache, forcing slow requests back to the origin.
suggestions.implementation: Investigate the Fastly CDN service configuration and the AEM Dispatcher cache purging strategy. The goal is to maximize the cache-hit ratio for the site's main document and static assets. Analyze the cache invalidation process to identify if it is overly aggressive or incorrectly configured.
suggestions.title: Investigate CDN Cache Misses to Reduce High TTFB

suggestions.description: The Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) image, `media_11d8f0a9f63483c3990309b297bf5c0d5763f5bf4.png`, is being loaded with a 'Low' browser priority. This is because it is missing the `fetchpriority='high'` attribute, causing an unnecessary delay of ~500ms in LCP time.
suggestions.implementation: In the JavaScript code responsible for decorating the hero block (likely within the `loadEager` function in `/scripts/scripts.js`), programmatically set `fetchpriority='high'` on the primary LCP `` element. Also ensure its `loading` attribute is set to 'eager'.
suggestions.title: Prioritize the LCP Image with fetchpriority='high'

suggestions.description: A large inline script (533 KB), identified as `inline@0`, is blocking the main thread during page load, contributing significantly to a Total Blocking Time of 2,760 ms and delaying LCP. Analysis shows 51% (270 KB) of its code is unused for the initial render. This long-running script is a primary cause of poor interactivity (INP) and a delayed LCP.
suggestions.implementation: Identify the source of the inline script (likely a third-party service such as a consent manager). Move this code into an external JavaScript file. Modify `scripts.js` to load this new file using the `loadDelayed` function, which ensures it executes after the page becomes interactive and doesn't block critical rendering.
suggestions.title: Defer execution of the large inline script to reduce main-thread blocking

suggestions.description: The Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) is delayed to 3.7s because the main hero image (e.g., `.../media_1463f710e8979...png`) is loaded with `loading="lazy"` and a default `fetchpriority="auto"`. This prevents the browser from discovering and downloading this critical resource early in the page load process.
suggestions.implementation: In `scripts.js`, within the `loadEager` function, find the logic that decorates the page's main hero image. Programmatically set its `loading` attribute to `"eager"` and its `fetchpriority` attribute to `"high"`. This will signal to the browser to download the LCP image immediately and with high priority, significantly improving LCP time.
suggestions.title: Prioritize the LCP image to accelerate rendering

suggestions.description:
The page loads multiple render-blocking stylesheets in the `<head>`, including over 118 KiB of CSS that is not used for the initial view. This blocks rendering and delays both First Contentful Paint (FCP) and the LCP of 3.7s. Files like `header.css`, `footer.css`, and other component styles are not needed for the above-the-fold content.

The Swiper JS library (`/scripts/vendor/swiper-bundle.min.js`), a 552 KB file, is loaded eagerly on the critical rendering path. This blocks the main thread and delays LCP, even if the slider component for which it is used is located below the fold.
suggestions.implementation:
- Audit the CSS loading strategy. Ensure only the minimal, critical CSS required for the above-the-fold content is loaded synchronously in the `<head>`. Move all other stylesheets (e.g., `lazy-styles.css`, `fonts.css`, `header.css`, `footer.css`, and CSS for below-the-fold blocks) to be loaded asynchronously using the `loadLazy` function in `scripts.js`.
- Identify the block that initializes the Swiper slider. Modify its JavaScript to load `swiper-bundle.min.js` asynchronously. This should be done by moving the initialization logic to the `loadLazy` phase in `scripts.js` and using a dynamic `import('/scripts/vendor/swiper-bundle.min.js')` call.
suggestions.title: Defer non-critical CSS to speed up initial rendering

suggestions.description: The initial request to `https://www.jcperreault.com` triggers a redirect to `https://www.jcperreault.com/`, adding a full network round-trip before the browser can start downloading the page content. This redirect delays the Time to First Byte (TTFB) and subsequent metrics like FCP and LCP by an estimated 750ms.
suggestions.implementation: Update the server or AEM Dispatcher configuration to handle requests for `https://www.jcperreault.com` directly without issuing a redirect. The server should respond with the HTML document for the root URL immediately, eliminating the extra network hop.
suggestions.title: Eliminate Redirect Chain to Improve Server Response Time

suggestions.description: A very long task is blocking the main thread for nearly 3 seconds (2946ms) at the very start of the page load. This severely delays the first paint and makes the page completely unresponsive, critically impacting INP, FCP, and LCP. This task is initiated by the eager JavaScript execution phase in `scripts.js`, which includes loading and running `web-components/web-components-bundle.js`.

suggestions.description:

suggestions.implementation:
- Audit the `/styles/output.css` file to identify the minimal set of CSS rules required to render the initial viewport (above-the-fold content). Move these critical styles into `/styles/styles.css`. Relocate all remaining non-critical styles (for below-the-fold content, interactive states, etc.) into `/styles/lazy-styles.css`, which should be loaded asynchronously.
- In `scripts.js`, move the loading of `web-components-bundle.js` from the `loadEager` phase to the `loadLazy` phase. This will defer its download and execution until after the initial page content has rendered, unblocking the LCP.
- Modify `scripts.js` to load non-critical stylesheets asynchronously. Specifically, ensure `/styles/lazy-styles.css` and CSS for blocks that always appear below the fold (like the footer) are loaded in the `loadLazy` phase by creating and appending a `<link rel="stylesheet">` element to the document head.
suggestions.title: Extract Critical CSS from `output.css` to Accelerate Rendering

suggestions.implementation: In a globally loaded stylesheet, such as `/styles.css`, apply a `min-height` to the container to reserve the necessary vertical space before its content loads. Add the following CSS rule: `#maruti-suzuki-india-business-channels { min-height: 91px; }`.
suggestions.title: Reserve space for asynchronously loaded content to prevent layout shift

suggestions.description: Critical first-party static assets are served with an extremely high Time To First Byte (TTFB) of over 700ms. This indicates a severe server-side performance issue or a consistent CDN cache miss, which delays the entire rendering process and negatively impacts LCP and INP. The delay is almost entirely in the 'Wait' (TTFB) phase for resources like `link-column.js` and `corp-footer.plain.html`.
suggestions.implementation: Investigate why static assets are not being served quickly from the Fastly CDN. Check for issues that could be breaking the cache, such as variance on query strings or request headers. If the issue is not cache-related, the AEM publish origin is likely the bottleneck. Profile and optimize the backend performance for generating these resources.
suggestions.title: Fix extreme server response times (TTFB) for static assets

suggestions.description:
The root URL `https://www.jmp.com/` performs a 301 redirect to `/en/home`, adding a full network round-trip delay of approximately 750ms before the main HTML document can be downloaded. This delays the entire page load, negatively impacting TTFB, FCP, and LCP.

Critical first-party assets, including the main HTML document (`/en/home`), JavaScript (`/scripts/scripts.js`), and CSS (`/styles/styles.css`), are frequently being served with a CDN `X-Cache: MISS`. This forces requests to go to the origin server, significantly increasing TTFB and overall load time for every user who encounters a miss.
suggestions.implementation:
- Configure the server or CDN (Fastly) to serve the content of `/en/home` directly from the root path (`/`). This eliminates the redirect and removes a blocking network request from the critical path. Ensure all canonical URLs and internal links are updated to point to the final destination to prevent this from recurring.
- Investigate the Fastly CDN configuration to determine the cause of the frequent cache misses. Check for incorrect cache-busting via query parameters, overly broad `Vary` headers, or flawed cache invalidation logic. Ensure that static, versioned assets have long `max-age` directives and that the CDN is properly configured to cache them.
suggestions.title: Eliminate initial redirect to improve server response time

suggestions.description: The Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) is significantly delayed to over 5.3s because the main hero image (`.../media_1f60ec7445022b185c063abee8849331ddefa9007.png...`) is incorrectly assigned `loading='lazy'`. This prevents the browser from discovering and downloading the most important visual element until late in the loading process.
suggestions.implementation: In `/scripts/scripts.js`, modify the logic within the `loadEager` function (or equivalent block decoration logic). Ensure that the main hero image for the page is identified and its attributes are programmatically set to `loading='eager'` and `fetchPriority='high'`. All other non-critical images should retain `loading='lazy'`.
suggestions.title: Prioritize the LCP image to accelerate visual loading

suggestions.description: A significant layout shift (CLS > 0.1) occurs when the navigation bar is loaded asynchronously. The `#nav` element's placeholder collapses or has no initial size, causing content below it to shift downwards once the navigation content is rendered.
suggestions.implementation: In `/styles/styles.css`, apply a fixed minimum height to the header element to reserve the required space before its content loads. Based on observation, add the rule: `header#nav { min-height: 191px; }`. This will prevent the page content from shifting when the navigation bar is populated.
suggestions.title: Reserve space for the navigation header to prevent layout shift

suggestions.description: The third-party OneTrust cookie consent banner is dynamically injected at the top of the page without reserving space, causing the entire page layout to be pushed down. This single event is responsible for a cumulative layout shift (CLS) score of 0.2488, which is significantly above the 'good' threshold of 0.1.
suggestions.implementation: To prevent the cookie banner from disrupting the page layout, modify its container styling to render as a non-intrusive overlay. In your main stylesheet (e.g., `styles/styles.css`), apply `position: fixed` and `z-index` to the banner's selector (e.g., `.onetrust-pc-dark-filter` or its container). This will remove it from the document flow, ensuring it appears over the content without shifting it.
suggestions.title: Prevent layout shift from OneTrust cookie banner

suggestions.description: Multiple heavy third-party scripts for analytics, support, and personalization are loaded eagerly, blocking the main thread for several seconds. These scripts, including Google Tag Manager, Ada Support (`static.ada.support`), Constructor.io (`cnstrc.com`), and OneTrust, delay the rendering of the main content (LCP) and cause long tasks that freeze the page, leading to poor INP.
suggestions.implementation: In `scripts/scripts.js`, locate the initialization calls for Google Tag Manager (GTM), Ada Support, Constructor.io (`bulk_fbNG3H.js` and `autocomplete.js`), and the OneTrust banner SDK. Move these calls from the eager or lazy loading phases into the `loadDelayed` function. This will postpone their download and execution until after the initial page content has loaded and become interactive.
suggestions.title: Defer non-critical third-party scripts to improve LCP and INP

suggestions.description: The initial request to `https://www.bulk.com` triggers a chain of two 301 redirects (`/` -> `/uk` -> `/uk/`), adding approximately 910ms of network latency before the browser can even begin to fetch the page HTML. This directly delays the Time to First Byte (TTFB), First Contentful Paint (FCP), and Largest Contentful Paint (LCP).
suggestions.implementation: Update your web server (e.g., Apache, Nginx) or CDN edge configuration to eliminate the intermediate redirect. Configure a single rule that redirects requests from `https://www.bulk.com/` directly to the final canonical URL `https://www.bulk.com/uk/`. Also, ensure all internal links and marketing campaigns point to the final destination URL to avoid triggering this redirect chain.
suggestions.title: Eliminate initial server redirects to reduce TTFB

suggestions.description:
The large Osano consent script (osano.js) is render-blocking, downloads over 1.1MB of data, and executes a 239ms task on the main thread before the LCP element is rendered. Findings code-inp-1, rules-lcp-1, and perf_observer-lcp-1 identify this as a primary bottleneck for LCP (est. ~500ms delay) and INP (est. ~200ms impact).

The third-party Talkdesk chat widget loads approximately 806 KB of resources, including non-optimal TTF fonts and a large 228 KB script (`main-vendor-BPY8…`), early in the page load. This consumes critical network bandwidth and CPU time, delaying LCP and causing long tasks that harm INP, as shown in findings har-inp-1 and rules-lcp-3.

Over 1MB of JavaScript is being downloaded from `www.googletagmanager.com` due to multiple, separate `gtag.js` initializations for different tracking IDs (AW-11334653569, G-V3CZKM4K6N, GT-KD23TWW). This adds significant network and CPU overhead during the critical rendering path, impacting LCP, TBT, and INP.
suggestions.implementation:
- In `/scripts/scripts.js`, move the initialization and loading of the Osano script (from `cmp.osano.com`) out of the main execution path or `loadEager` phase. Instead, load it within the `loadDelayed` function. This will defer its network request and long execution task until after the page has rendered and become interactive.
- The chat widget is not essential for the initial render. In `scripts.js`, move its initialization script from the eager/lazy loading phase into the `loadDelayed` function. To further improve INP, implement an interaction facade: show a static "Chat" button placeholder and only load the full `talkdeskchatsdk.js` script when a user clicks it.
- Consolidate all tracking tags (e.g., Google Analytics, Google Ads) into a single Google Tag Manager (GTM) container. Audit the tags within the new container to remove any that are redundant. Ensure the single GTM container script is loaded asynchronously via the `loadDelayed` function in `scripts.js` to prevent it from impacting page load performance.
suggestions.title: Defer the Osano Consent Manager script to improve LCP and INP

suggestions.description: The LCP image (`.../media_11d8f0a9f63483c3990309b297bf5c0d5763f5bf4.png`) is critical for page speed perception, but the browser is downloading it with a 'Low' priority. This is because AEM lazily loads images by default, which is incorrect for an above-the-fold hero image, contributing to a slow LCP of 3.2s.
suggestions.implementation: In `scripts.js`, within the decoration logic for the block containing the LCP image (likely a hero banner, executed in the `loadEager` phase), programmatically identify the main `` element. Set its `loading` attribute to `"eager"` and, crucially, set its `fetchpriority` attribute to `"high"`. This signals the browser to download the image immediately with high priority.
suggestions.title: Set high fetch priority for the LCP image to accelerate its loading

suggestions.description: A significant layout shift (CLS of 0.13) occurs when the web fonts ('Raleway', 'Libre Franklin') load. This is caused by two issues: the fonts use `font-display: auto`, which causes a flash of invisible text, and the size of the fallback font does not match the web font, causing a visible reflow when the swap happens.
suggestions.implementation: In `/styles/fonts.css`, modify the `@font-face` rules for 'Raleway' and 'Libre Franklin'. First, add `font-display: swap;` to prevent invisible text. Second, create a fallback font definition using `@font-face` with a `local()` source (e.g., Arial). Use the `size-adjust`, `ascent-override`, `descent-override`, and `line-gap-override` CSS properties on this fallback rule to match its dimensions to the web font, minimizing the size difference during the swap and reducing CLS.
suggestions.title: Stabilize layout by optimizing web font loading and fallbacks

suggestions.description: A significant layout shift of 0.516 is occurring because content is being inserted asynchronously, pushing existing elements like the `.button-container` down by 134 pixels without any space reserved for it. This is a primary cause of the poor CLS score.
suggestions.implementation: In the CSS file for the block that contains the `.button-container`, apply a `min-height` to the block's main wrapper element. The height should be sufficient to accommodate the content that is loaded asynchronously. This will reserve the necessary vertical space before rendering, preventing the layout shift.
suggestions.title: Reserve space for dynamic content to prevent major layout shifts

suggestions.description: A large portion of the Cumulative Layout Shift is caused by web fonts ('Acceptance Bold', 'Acceptance Regular') replacing fallback fonts with different dimensions. This causes text blocks like `#__ccb_text` and other elements to reflow, contributing significantly to the poor CLS score of 0.22.
suggestions.implementation: In `/styles/fonts.css`, ensure all `@font-face` rules include the `font-display: swap;` descriptor. In `/styles/styles.css`, for each custom font, define a corresponding `@font-face` rule for a web-safe fallback font (e.g., Arial) and use the `size-adjust`, `ascent-override`, and `descent-override` CSS properties to match its metrics to the primary web font. This will minimize the size difference during the swap.
suggestions.title: Mitigate font-swapping layout shifts using size-adjusted fallbacks

suggestions.description:
Numerous third-party scripts for analytics, marketing, and session replay (Adobe DTM, Google Tag Manager, FullStory, Facebook, TikTok, `beacon.min.js`) are loaded in the page `<head>` or early in the page load. They create significant network and main-thread contention, blocking rendering, delaying LCP by over 1 second, and causing long tasks that harm INP.

Over 2.4MB of JavaScript is downloaded, with a significant portion being unused. Major contributors are third-party tools like Google Tag Manager (269KB unused) and Adobe Launch (142KB unused). This unused code is still parsed and compiled, consuming CPU time and contributing to high Total Blocking Time and poor INP.
suggestions.implementation:
- In `/scripts/scripts.js`, move the loader functions for all non-essential third-party scripts from the `<head>`, `loadEager`, or `loadLazy` phases into the `loadDelayed` function. This includes the loaders for Adobe DTM/Launch (`launch-*.min.js`), Google Tag Manager (`gtm.js`), FullStory (`fs.js`), Facebook Pixel (`fbevents.js`), TikTok Pixel (`main.*.js`), and the New Relic monitoring script (`beacon.min.js`).
- Perform a comprehensive audit of the configurations within your third-party management tools, primarily Google Tag Manager and Adobe Launch. Identify and remove any tags, triggers, and variables that are obsolete, redundant, or not used on this site. This is a configuration change within the vendor's UI, not a code change in the repository.
suggestions.title: Defer non-essential third-party scripts to improve LCP and INP

suggestions.description:
A 3.2-second long task, initiated by the `loadEager` function in `scripts.js`, blocks the main thread at the very start of the page load. This severely delays all rendering and interactivity, contributing significantly to poor LCP and INP.

A large JavaScript file for video functionality, `video.min.js` (198 KB), is loaded with high priority during the initial page load. This script is not needed until a user interacts with a video, and its eager loading competes for bandwidth with critical LCP resources and blocks the main thread.

A 'first-visit' modal, loaded via `form.js`, initiates a long-running request chain that introduces a sequential delay of over 20 seconds. This consumes critical network and CPU resources during the initial load, delaying LCP and interactivity.
suggestions.implementation:
- Analyze the synchronous code executed by the `loadEager` function in `/scripts/scripts.js`. Identify the source of the 3.2-second long task and refactor it. Break the long-running script into smaller, asynchronous tasks using techniques like `setTimeout(..., 0)` or `scheduler.yield()` to yield to the main thread, allowing the browser to render content and respond to input sooner.
- Refactor how videos are loaded. Instead of loading `/scripts/video.min.js` upfront, implement a video facade. Display a lightweight placeholder (an image with a play icon) initially. Load the full `video.min.js` script and initialize the video player only when a user clicks on this placeholder.
- Modify the site's main script file, `/scripts/scripts.js`. Move the code responsible for triggering the load and display of the first-visit modal out of the eager execution path and into the `loadDelayed` function. This ensures the modal only loads after the main page content has been rendered and is interactive.
suggestions.title: Break up 3.2-second long task at page start

suggestions.description: The primary above-the-fold hero image, a likely LCP element, is being loaded with default or low priority because it's missing critical attributes. Findings indicate it may even be lazy-loaded, which severely delays its discovery and download, harming LCP.
suggestions.implementation: In the AEM component or the `decorateMain`/`loadEager` phase of `/scripts/scripts.js`, locate the main hero image element (e.g., the `` tag for `WC_CLP_Hero.jpg` or `.../2603-BSbyBR-Site-MattressCollectionHP-420x546.avif`). Ensure its HTML attributes are set to `loading="eager"` and `fetchpriority="high"`. Remove any `loading="lazy"` attribute from this specific image.
suggestions.title: Prioritize the LCP hero image for faster loading

suggestions.description: The OneTrust cookie consent script (`otSDKStub.js` from `cdn.cookielaw.org`) is loaded synchronously in the document `<head>`. This blocks the browser from parsing the rest of the page and initiates a long chain of network requests, delaying FCP, LCP, and interactivity.
suggestions.implementation: Remove the synchronous `<script>` tag for `https://cdn.cookielaw.org/scripttemplates/otSDKStub.js` from the HTML `<head>`. Instead, load the script asynchronously by calling it from within the `loadDelayed` function in `/scripts/scripts.js`. This will prevent it from blocking the initial page render.
suggestions.title: Defer the render-blocking OneTrust cookie script

suggestions.description:
The main stylesheet, `output.css`, is a large, render-blocking resource that takes over 1 second to load, delaying the Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) by a similar amount. The page also loads multiple other stylesheets synchronously in the `<head>`, including CSS for the header, footer, and a misconfigured `lazy-styles.css`, all of which block the initial render.

Multiple JavaScript modules, including `global.js`, `web-components-bundle.js`, and `commerce.js`, are loaded as render-blocking scripts in the HTML `<head>`. This is an anti-pattern that delays parsing, resource discovery, and the execution of the main `scripts.js` file, which orchestrates the LCP render.
suggestions.implementation:
- Refactor the CSS loading strategy. First, split `output.css` into a minimal, critical CSS file containing only above-the-fold styles. Inline this critical CSS or load it as a small, blocking stylesheet. Move all non-critical styles (for below-the-fold content, header, footer, etc.) into `lazy-styles.css`. Finally, ensure `lazy-styles.css` is loaded asynchronously by moving its `<link>` tag out of the HTML `<head>` and loading it via JavaScript in the `loadLazy` phase within `scripts.js`.
- Remove all blocking `<script type="module">` tags for application logic from the HTML `<head>`. Instead, manage their loading from within `/scripts/scripts.js` using dynamic `import()`. Import scripts that are critical for the initial viewport within the `loadEager` phase. Defer all other scripts to be imported in the `loadLazy` or `loadDelayed` phases.
suggestions.title: Split and Defer Non-Critical CSS to Unblock Rendering

suggestions.description:
A multi-step redirect chain is delaying the initial HTML document response by approximately 750 ms. This significantly increases the Time to First Byte (TTFB), which in turn delays the entire page rendering process and negatively impacts LCP and FCP.

Critical resources, including the main HTML document and numerous JavaScript files, are not being served from the CDN cache, as indicated by `X-Cache: MISS` headers. This forces requests to go to the origin server, increasing TTFB and delaying the start of the entire rendering process, with an estimated LCP impact of 300ms.
suggestions.implementation:
- Consolidate the redirect chain into a single, direct server-side redirect. Investigate the web server (e.g., Apache, Nginx) or CDN configuration to combine any sequential redirects (e.g., HTTP to HTTPS, then non-www to www) into a single 301 redirect. This will remove an unnecessary network round trip.
- Investigate and resolve the root cause of CDN cache misses. Check the CDN and server configurations for issues that break cacheability, such as: inconsistent `Vary` headers, unique query parameters being added to static resource URLs, or an overly aggressive cache purging strategy during deployments. Ensure static assets have consistent URLs and cache-friendly headers to maximize the CDN hit rate.
suggestions.title: Eliminate Redirect Chain to Reduce Server Delay

suggestions.description: The Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) image (`.../media_1941fe7d5d6e...`) is being loaded with `loading="lazy"` by default. This causes the browser to assign it a low priority, delaying its discovery and download until after other resources, impacting LCP by an estimated 500ms.
suggestions.implementation: In `scripts.js`, within the `loadEager` function, programmatically identify the LCP image element (typically the main image in the hero block). Update its attributes to ensure it is prioritized by the browser by setting `loading="eager"` and `fetchpriority="high"`.
suggestions.title: Prioritize the LCP Image for Faster Loading

suggestions.description: The main document and critical assets like `scripts.js` and `styles.css` are frequently not being served from the CDN, indicated by 'X-Cache: MISS' headers. This results in a high Time to First Byte (TTFB), for example 343ms for a static file like `lazy-styles.css`, which slows down the entire page rendering process.
suggestions.implementation: Investigate the AEM publishing workflow and CDN cache configuration. The `Cache-Control: max-age=7200, must-revalidate` header found on static assets like `scripts.js` and `styles.css` may be causing premature revalidation. Adjust the caching policy to ensure a high cache HIT ratio for these assets, which should be treated as immutable.
suggestions.title: Fix CDN Cache Misses for Critical First-Party Assets

suggestions.description:
The Real User Monitoring script, `datadog-rum.js`, is 981 KB and is loaded and executed before the Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) element is rendered. This blocks the main thread, consumes significant network bandwidth, and severely delays page rendering.

Multiple heavy third-party scripts for analytics and marketing (Google Tag Manager, Google Analytics, Facebook Events, ZoomInfo, InstantSearch.js) are loading early. This causes long request chains, significant main-thread blocking (e.g., a 245ms long task from `gtm.js`), and adds hundreds of kilobytes of unused code, which harms INP, TBT, and LCP.

A third-party widget from `pearsonpols.my.site.com` is slow to load, with high aggregate TTFB (over 4.7s) and large script downloads (692 KB across 17 requests). This blocks the network and main thread during page load, harming both LCP and INP.
suggestions.implementation:
- In `/scripts/scripts.js`, locate the code that loads `datadog-rum.js`. Move this script's loading logic from the eager-loading phase (e.g., `loadEager`) into the `loadDelayed` function. This will ensure the script only loads after the page has become interactive, removing it from the critical rendering path.
- In `/scripts/scripts.js`, ensure all non-essential third-party scripts are loaded in the `loadDelayed` phase. This includes scripts for Google Tag Manager (`gtm.js`), Google Analytics (`gtag/js`), Facebook (`fbevents.js`), ZoomInfo, and InstantSearch.js (`instantsearch.production.min.js`). Move their initialization from any eager or lazy loading blocks to the `loadDelayed` function.
- Move the initialization script for the Pearson/Salesforce widget into the `loadDelayed` function within `scripts.js`. To further improve user experience, replace the widget's initial embed code with a static placeholder element (a 'facade') that only loads the full widget script when the user clicks on it.
suggestions.title: Defer the Datadog RUM script to prevent render blocking

suggestions.description: A 1.4 MB animated GIF located at `/media_1af1585bb66e4c6efcc7ee8249117762ac1c03c53.gif` is being loaded. Its large size consumes excessive network bandwidth and takes over 18 seconds to download on slower connections, delaying the overall page load and impacting LCP.
suggestions.implementation: Convert the animated GIF at `https://nursing.maryville.edu/media_1af1585bb66e4c6efcc7ee8249117762ac1c03c53.gif` into a modern video format like WebM or MP4. Replace the `` tag in the HTML with a `
suggestions.title: Replace large 1.4 MB animated GIF with an optimized video

suggestions.description:
The page's LCP is severely delayed by a slow backend response from a critical first-party API. The request to `https://ae.hm.com/graphql?...` has a Time to First Byte (TTFB) of 1009ms, which blocks the rendering of primary page content.

The initial page load is slowed by a redirect chain, adding approximately 750ms of delay before the server starts sending the HTML document. This directly increases Time to First Byte (TTFB) and delays LCP.
suggestions.implementation:
- Investigate the performance of the backend service handling the GraphQL endpoint at `/graphql`. Focus on optimizing server-side logic, improving database query efficiency, and implementing or correcting server-level caching strategies for this API response to reduce its TTFB to under 200ms.
- Investigate and remove the redirect chain for the entry URL. This is often managed in AEM through redirect maps at the CDN level or web server configuration. Ensure the URL `https://ae.hm.com` resolves directly with a 200 OK status code without any intermediate HTTP 301 or 302 redirects.
suggestions.title: Optimize Slow Backend Response for Critical GraphQL API

suggestions.description:
A large video player script, `video.min.js` (157 KB) from `vjs.zencdn.net`, is loaded synchronously in the critical path. It blocks rendering, contributes over 1200ms of delay, and causes a 329ms long task, severely impacting LCP (currently 5.2s).

The page's initial render (FCP and LCP) is delayed because 18 stylesheets are loaded as render-blocking resources in the document `<head>`. This includes non-critical styles for below-the-fold content like the footer and lazy-loaded components.
suggestions.implementation:
- Implement a 'facade' pattern for video elements. Instead of loading `video.min.js` in the `<head>` or during the initial `loadEager` phase, replace the video player with a lightweight placeholder (e.g., a thumbnail image with a play icon). Load the `video.min.js` script and initialize the player only when a user clicks on this facade. This change will remove the script from the LCP critical path.
- Separate critical and non-critical CSS. Consolidate styles for non-essential or below-the-fold components (e.g., `/blocks/header/hmns/header.css`, `/blocks/footer/hmns/footer.css`) into a single non-critical stylesheet like `lazy-styles.css`. Remove the `<link>` tags for these stylesheets from the HTML `<head>` and instead load them asynchronously using the `loadLazy` function in `scripts.js`.
suggestions.title: Defer Loading of the Blocking Video Player Script

suggestions.description: Multiple third-party analytics, advertising, and session replay scripts are loaded eagerly, creating a long sequential request chain and executing long tasks (e.g., a 445ms task from GTM). This blocks the main thread, delaying LCP by over 1000ms and causing high INP.
suggestions.implementation: In `/scripts/scripts.js`, move the initialization logic for all non-essential third-party scripts into the `loadDelayed()` function. This includes Google Tag Manager (GTM-5TX6KPZ), Facebook Pixel (`fbevents.js`), Exponea (`exponea.min.js`), and Clarity (`clarity.js`). This will execute them after the page is interactive, freeing up the main thread during the critical load time.
suggestions.title: Defer Non-Essential Third-Party Scripts to Improve LCP and INP

suggestions.description: Real users are experiencing a high Time to First Byte (TTFB) of over 1.1 seconds, which adds a significant delay before the page can even start rendering. Analysis shows this is caused by frequent CDN cache misses for the main HTML document and critical static assets like `/styles/styles.css` and `/scripts/scripts.js`.
suggestions.implementation: Escalate to the infrastructure team to investigate the Fastly CDN and origin server configuration. Analyze Fastly cache hit ratios and the origin's `Cache-Control` headers (e.g., `must-revalidate`). The goal is to increase the cache HIT ratio for the main document and immutable static assets to ensure a consistently low TTFB.
suggestions.title: Fix high TTFB by optimizing CDN cache configuration

suggestions.description:
The page's LCP of 4.26s is primarily caused by the slow download of the LCP element itself, an image (`.../media_1e16ce0980916505f1578875215ad6336d2cdcfac.webp`). This image is 159KB, and its download takes 4.15 seconds, blocking the completion of the main content paint.

The LCP image is not being prioritized correctly. The document `<head>` uses `<link rel="preload">` for images, which is an anti-pattern in AEM EDS that can cause resource contention. In some cases, the LCP image is even downloaded with 'Low' priority.
suggestions.implementation:
- Before uploading to the AEM author environment, re-export the source image for `media_1e16ce0980916505f1578875215ad6336d2cdcfac.webp`. Use more aggressive compression settings to reduce its file size significantly (aim for under 100KB) for mobile viewports, which will shorten its download time.
- First, remove all `<link rel="preload">` tags for images from the document `<head>`. Then, in the `loadEager` function within `/scripts/scripts.js`, identify the LCP image element and programmatically set its `fetchpriority` attribute to `"high"` to signal its importance to the browser.
suggestions.title: Reduce LCP by compressing the large hero image

suggestions.description:
The initial rendering of the page is significantly delayed by an excessive number of 27 render-blocking stylesheets loaded in the document `<head>`. This includes non-critical CSS for below-the-fold components like the footer and carousels, which should not block the LCP.

Several non-critical JavaScript files for UI components are loaded in the `loadEager` phase, unnecessarily bloating the critical path by over 300KB. This includes scripts for the header navigation (`header-nav.js`), scroll animations (`locomotive-scroll.min.js`), and carousels (`slick-1.8.1.min.js`), which all block the main thread and delay LCP.

A large JSON file, `query-index.json` (over 348KB), is downloaded with high priority during the initial page load for the site search feature. This consumes significant network bandwidth on the critical path, slowing down the download of essential resources like the LCP image.
suggestions.implementation:
- Refactor the CSS loading strategy to align with AEM EDS best practices. First, consolidate all essential, above-the-fold styles into `/styles/styles.css`. Second, move all non-critical and block-specific styles into `/styles/lazy-styles.css`. Finally, ensure `lazy-styles.css` is loaded asynchronously by calling it from the `loadLazy` function in `/scripts/scripts.js` and remove the individual block stylesheet links from the `<head>`.
- In `/scripts/scripts.js`, review the `loadEager` function and move the dynamic imports for non-critical UI components to the `loadLazy` function. Specifically, relocate the loading for `header-nav.js`, `locomotive-scroll.min.js`, and `slick-1.8.1.min.js`.
- In `/scripts/scripts.js`, locate the code that fetches `query-index.json`. Move this fetch call from the eager-loading phase into the `loadLazy` function. For an even better experience, modify the logic to trigger the download only when a user first interacts with the search input field.
suggestions.title: Eliminate render-blocking CSS by consolidating stylesheets

suggestions.description:
The video player script, `/scripts/video.min.js`, is loaded eagerly and executes a ~2-second long task on the main thread. This blocks the browser from rendering content and responding to user input, severely degrading both the Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) and Interaction to Next Paint (INP).

The script for the carousel component, `/blocks/cndl-carousel/cndl-carousel.js`, is being loaded and executed eagerly before the LCP is rendered. This adds unnecessary JavaScript execution to the critical rendering path.
suggestions.implementation:
- Instead of loading `/scripts/video.min.js` eagerly in the `loadEager` phase, implement a video facade. Replace the video player element with a lightweight placeholder (a thumbnail image with a play icon). The full `video.min.js` script should only be loaded and initialized when a user clicks this placeholder. This change should be implemented in the video component's logic and the site's main `/scripts/scripts.js` file.
- Ensure the carousel component is lazy-loaded. In `/scripts/scripts.js`, verify that the logic to decorate and initialize the carousel block is located within the `loadLazy` function, not `loadEager`. If the carousel is currently in the first section of the page, consider moving it to a lower section to prevent eager loading.
suggestions.title: Defer Video Player Script Execution to Resolve 2-Second Long Task

suggestions.description: Synchronously loaded Google reCAPTCHA scripts are severely harming performance. They are loaded from the document `<head>`, block rendering, consume over 4.5MB of network bandwidth, and execute long tasks (e.g., 452ms) on the main thread. This delays the Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) and hurts Interaction to Next Paint (INP).
suggestions.implementation: In `/scripts/scripts.js`, move the loading and initialization logic for all Google reCAPTCHA scripts (`enterprise.js` and `recaptcha__en.js`) from the `loadEager` phase into the `loadDelayed` function. Also, ensure no `<script>` tags for reCAPTCHA are present in the initial HTML `<head>`. This will prevent them from blocking the initial page render and executing during the critical loading period.
suggestions.title: Defer Google reCAPTCHA Scripts to Improve LCP and INP

suggestions.description: The page experiences a severe Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS) of up to 0.268. This is primarily caused when the custom web font `gotham-book.woff2` loads and replaces the system font used for the main heading (`<h1 id="brewed-perfect-every-sip-every-time">`), causing a 94px height change.
suggestions.implementation: In `/styles/styles.css`, define a new `@font-face` rule for a local fallback font (e.g., Arial). Use the `size-adjust`, `ascent-override`, and `descent-override` CSS descriptors within this rule to precisely match the metrics of the `gotham-book` web font. This ensures the space reserved by the fallback font is identical to the space the final font will occupy, eliminating the layout shift. Ensure `font-display: swap` is also used.
suggestions.title: Stabilize Page Heading by Matching Fallback Font Metrics
